newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to revise liquor tax system in 97/98 - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to revise liquor tax system in 97/98 - MOF.

text.p: Japan will revise its liquor taxation system in the fiscal year starting next April in line with the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) ruling that Japan's taxes discriminate against imported liquor, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday.

Concerning the separation of the MOF's financial inspection and supervision units, Mitsuzuka told a news conference that there was nearly a consensus now in the government and within the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) about the idea of separating the two units from the ministry simultaneously.
Some LDP politicians have been calling on the government to hive off only the inspection unit.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has made remarks in favour of simultaneous separation of these two units, Mitsuzuka said.
"The remark from the top government official is important, and I think his idea is now spreading (throughout the government and the LDP)," he said.
Mitsuzuka said he intends to complete a final plan for reforming the Finance Ministry after the current parliament session ends on December 18.

On Japan's liquor tax system, Mitsuzuka said a revised system must be implemented next fiscal year after measures are drawn up to help domestic liquor makers cope with possible damage to their business stemming from the change in liquor taxes.
"Japan will faithfully carry out the international pledge it made after the WTO ruling," he said.
